Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (1,2,4).

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,2,7).
Going to (2,4,7) would leave number 16 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (4,2,7).
The line must go to (6,2,7): to (4,4,7) is number 21, which comes later.
Going to (7,2,6) leaves no safe move afterwards; going to (6,4,7) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (6,1,6).
The line must go to (7,2,6): to (6,1,4) is number 18, which comes later.
Going to (7,4,6) would cut off a group of 7 cells. So the line goes to (7,2,4).
Going to (7,2,2) would leave both cell (7,4,2) and cell (6,2,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (6,1,4).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,1,2).
Cell (6,2,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (7,2,2).
Going to (6,4,7) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (7,6,6).
Going to number 20 would leave both cell (6,7,6) and cell (6,4,7) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (6,7,6).
Going to (4,7,6) would force the line onto number 23 before its turn. So the line goes to (6,6,7).
The line must go to (6,4,7): to (4,6,7) is number 24, which comes later.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
